entries.title: TEDxBoston
entries.text: 2023. How AI can make rare diseases rarer.

entries.title: Find the business's core learning problem first
entries.text: Every industry has one quantity whose improvement compounds. AI earns its budget by moving that number, not by adding a chatbot. Yield is a learning problem: each device built carries data on why the next will pass or fail. The forecast is the product. Weather, load and price forecasts sit under every trade and dispatch. In a ramp-up, AI's first job is to shorten the learning curve on yield and time to qualification. Decades of trial and field data are the science; the job is making them compound across seasons.

entries.title: Context is the moat; models are a commodity
entries.text: Everyone can rent a frontier model. What is scarce is trusted, permissioned, versioned context an agent can act on. A shared context layer is the direct answer to what should be centralized. Map data to the process it describes; structured and unstructured knowledge behind one permission model. Model choice should be a routing decision you can change in an afternoon. The context layer is the center of gravity.

entries.title: Govern by design, so the safe path is the fast path
entries.text: Controls belong in the platform: identity, guardrails, logging and change control, not a review gate at the end. Validated by design: locked model versions and risk-based assurance built into the platform. Grid, markets and ratemaking each carry their own rules; the platform enforces them. Process IP is the crown jewel, and every architecture choice is tested against leaking it. Autonomy is a permission earned per workflow, never a setting you turn on.

entries.title: Risk-tier every model
entries.text: A meeting summarizer and a model that sets a process parameter do not deserve the same review. Proportion is what lets you move fast where it is safe. Four tiers, from direct product-quality impact (full validation) down to productivity tools. A model that shapes a market offer or a rate filing gets a different review from a summarizer. Tiered review from email assistants to models recommending furnace setpoints. Authority tiers decide what an agent may read, propose or execute.

entries.title: Build once, reuse many times
entries.text: A platform justifies itself only when the fifth team ships in a fraction of the first team's effort. Shared data, MLOps and validation first; then every plant and planner reuses them. If the same capability is rebuilt in three teams, that is a platform gap, not a talent gap. Composable and compostable: modular parts, each replaceable in 18 months. Golden paths: the first delivery is a paved road with one solution on it.

entries.title: Central standards, federated delivery
entries.text: The enterprise owns architecture, security and reusable platforms. Business units own their data and outcomes. The line is drawn explicitly. A federated organization with one standard and clear decision rights. Centralize the rules of the road; federate ownership of domain data. Explicit RACI between the platform team and the domains it serves.

entries.title: Measure value created, not models built
entries.text: A model matters only when it changes a decision: a bid, a work order, a capital plan. Start from the decision and its owner. Forecasts are measured in procedures served; a stockout is a delayed procedure. Decisions, not models. Every initiative names the decision it changes. Adoption, quality, reuse and speed, each traced to margin, revenue or customer outcome. Evaluation is the product, not the QA step.

entries.title: Every answer has a token bill
entries.text: Inference cost per agentic workflow is rising. The harness, caching and routing matter more than the model's horsepower. Most of the token bill is avoidable with context, caching and routing. Cost control is a platform capability every team inherits for free.
